transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-04-06
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Larkspur - Head of Security), Marcus Li (Larkspur - Platform Eng), Jenna Ortiz (Larkspur - PM)

Summary: weekly pilot check-in; focus on SSO, audit logs, retention policy, SOC2 artifacts, and a review of pilot telemetry. Transcription may include minor errors and mis-hearings.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll run about 45 minutes. quick status: SSO, logs, retention, SOC2. Priya, do you want to start with security takeaways?
[00:45] Priya Rao: yeah thanks. on SSO we imported the SAML metadata but SCIM provisioning is failing for auto-assign. certain attributes like employeeNumber and officeLocation are not in the SCIM payload. so users are created but not mapped to our internal groups.
[01:20] Ethan Park: okay sounds like a mapping issue. the SCIM we emit is the standard urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User with optional extension attributes. we can add custom mapping rules in the pilot tenant. please drop a sample manifest in the ticket and i'll adjust the mappings.
[02:05] Marcus Li: i'll do that. second item: audit logs. we need raw API access logs for 90 days searchable, plus an archival push for 7 years to our legal archive. can Redwood forward logs to Splunk HEC in near real-time?
[02:40] Maya Chen: yes — we support push to Splunk HEC, S3, or syslog. hosted tenants get 90 days in-console; for long-term retention we recommend forwarding to your S3 archive. on Dedicated we can set the forwarding up directly and meet retention SLAs in contract.
[03:15] Priya Rao: about PII—are request bodies redacted by default? our policy forbids storing user content in plaintext in logs.
[03:34] Ethan Park: default pipeline redacts sensitive fields and full request bodies for configured endpoints; metadata (user-id, request path, timestamps) is kept. for the pilot we can enable a more restrictive redaction policy. we'll circulate the compliance matrix that specifies which fields are redacted.
[04:10] Jenna Ortiz: from product side we do rely on some request payloads to debug model outputs during the POC. is there a way to give our SREs access to full-text logs but keep them masked for others?
[04:32] Maya Chen: yes, we can implement role-based access controls: grant a specific RBAC role to your SREs with full-text view, while others see masked content. for higher assurance we can export full-text to an encrypted S3 bucket in your account where only your team has access.
[05:00] Marcus Li: KMS question — do you support customer-managed keys? we prefer HSM-backed keys for at-rest encryption.
[05:15] Ethan Park: for Dedicated and Private yes — BYOK supported, KMS integrations available, and HSM via our partners is possible. hosted is managed keys by default but we can evaluate a dedicated key configuration for enterprise pilots.
[06:00] Priya Rao: timeline needed — we have a security review with legal in three weeks and will need SOC 2 evidence. can you share SOC 2 Type II artifacts?
[06:20] Maya Chen: we will share the SOC 2 Type II report and a controls mapping to your checklist. i'll upload to the shared drive by Friday and flag any open remediation items.
[07:05] Jenna Ortiz: pilot metrics quick review: we were targeting p50 < 150ms and 5M tokens/month cost estimates. what are we seeing in the staging runs?
[07:30] Ethan Park: current telemetry: p50 ~138ms with default batching; p95 ~420ms under the worst observed spike. token consumption was slightly higher due to tokenization. we found a normalization mismatch inflating tokens by about 6%. we can push a tokenization config update to the pilot to reduce usage.
[08:05] Marcus Li: please share tokenizer config and any pre-processing script; we'll run it through our pipeline. also, does quantization or model variant change audit log format or storage?
[08:28] Maya Chen: no, model variant doesn't change audit schema. logs always include metadata plus an identifier for the model variant. quantization affects compute not telemetry.
[09:00] Priya Rao: on legal hold — we need the ability to freeze deletion for a set of users or objects for litigation. is legal hold supported?
[09:18] Ethan Park: legal hold is supported for Dedicated/Private via protected archive buckets. on Hosted we can emulate legal hold by flagging objects and moving them to a protected S3 bucket with extended retention — this path requires manual workflow initially.
[10:00] Jenna Ortiz: who owns the process to enable legal hold — customer or Redwood support?
[10:12] Maya Chen: policy changes require a small support runbook initially; once formalized we can expose legal-hold controls in the console for Dedicated customers.
[12:00] Marcus Li: logging format question — do you include request raw headers? we need to mask Authorization headers but still record the fact an auth event occurred.
[12:22] Ethan Park: we strip Authorization header values in logs and store a hashed token fingerprint for correlation, along with status codes and latency. we can also forward a separate auth audit stream if you want fine-grained auth telemetry into your identity store.
[14:00] Priya Rao: audit log integrity — do you provide immutable logs or signing? for compliance we prefer append-only signed logs.
[14:18] Maya Chen: we offer append-only logs for Dedicated/Private and we can configure signing and immutability. for hosted we have an integrity window and can work on extended features via contract.
[16:00] Jenna Ortiz: operational question — who has admin access in the pilot tenant? currently Marcus and I both had admin, but Priya's team needs an auditor role.
[16:18] Maya Chen: we can create RBAC roles: admin, ops, auditor, read-only, and custom roles. we'll provision an auditor role scoped to logs and compliance artifacts and not to model rollouts.
[18:00] Marcus Li: okay. about exporting console actions to our change management system — can console audit events be pushed to our ticketing tool?
[18:20] Ethan Park: yes — webhook or S3 export. we can also include a mapping from console events to your ticket fields.
[20:00] Priya Rao: testing plan for SSO: we'll do a SCIM provisioning smoke test and a SAML sign-on validation. what's the recommended schedule for the workshop?
[20:25] Maya Chen: let's do a 60-min workshop next Tuesday at 10am PT. Ethan will run it and walk through SAML metadata, SCIM claims, and test users.
[22:00] Marcus Li: perfect. i'll add example LDAP attributes and our IdP metadata in the ticket.
[24:00] Ethan Park: i'll prepare a sample mapping table and a small SCIM test harness for you to run. i'll also include the sample metadata file and steps to capture SAML traces.
[26:00] Jenna Ortiz: about compliance docs — will you include a data flow diagram showing where logs live and how they're forwarded? we need that for our legal review.
[26:18] Maya Chen: yes, we'll include a data flow diagram and a narrative mapping to SOC 2 controls.
[28:00] Priya Rao: retention windows: we prefer 90 days of hot logs, 7 years cold archive, and ability to run e-discovery. can Redwood support e-discovery queries across the archive?
[28:22] Ethan Park: yes for archived S3 we can either provide a search index or grant you a read-only bucket for your e-discovery tooling. search across the archive is available as an add-on.
[30:00] Marcus Li: billing and access question — our finance team wants per-token cost breakout and per-route cost. can we get a sample billing report from the pilot?
[30:18] Maya Chen: we can share token-level billing and route-level cost in the Console. i'll attach a pilot billing export and sample query to the shared drive.
[32:00] Jenna Ortiz: any blockers on Redwood side to get the SOC 2 doc and SSO playbook to us this week?
[32:12] Maya Chen: no blockers. i'll upload the SOC2 Type II and the compliance matrix by Friday. Ethan will upload the SSO/SCIM playbook and tokenizer config by Thursday.
[34:00] Priya Rao: small note — please label the SOC2 docs with the date and the auditor name; our legal reviews the auditor identity.
[34:18] Maya Chen: noted. will include auditor and reporting period.
[36:00] Marcus Li: regarding the read-only audit log export into our staging Splunk — what's the mechanism? HEC token?
[36:15] Ethan Park: we'll provision a HEC endpoint in your staging and push batched events; it's near-real time with <30s lag for typical throughput. we'll send HEC token provisioning steps and firewall IPs.
[38:00] Jenna Ortiz: are there any known limitations in the pilot tenant that might affect our load test?
[38:20] Maya Chen: pilot tenant has standard limits; we can temporarily increase throughput for scheduled tests. we'll need to coordinate times. there may be small differences in routing behavior vs production but nothing material to the telemetry.
[40:00] Priya Rao: last security question — do you support SAML assertion encryption in transit and signed artifacts?
[40:15] Ethan Park: yes signed assertions and encryption are supported; we'll include an example of metadata with encryption enabled in the playbook.
[42:00] Maya Chen: cool. recap of action items and owners in the ticket shortly. i'll also send calendar invite for the SSO workshop. any final comments?
[43:00] Priya Rao: just that we appreciate the clarity on redaction and legal hold approaches. once we have SOC2 and SCIM mapping fixed we should be unblocked.
[44:00] Marcus Li: thanks all. i'll start the SCIM test and update the ticket.
[45:00] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up on the items.

Notes: Minor transcription mismatches: "Redwood dedicate" interpreted in a couple places; "SCIM manifest" vs "SCIM mapping". Shared artifacts referenced: SOC2 report (shared drive link), SSO playbook (redwood-assets/sso-playbook.pdf), tokenizer config (attachment).

End transcript.
